questions.text: Right now, how does your body feel?

options.text: Still and peaceful — no tension at all
Alert and steady — I'm focused and ready
Loose and comfortable — like I could melt into my chair
Tense — my shoulders, jaw, or stomach feel tight
Heavy — my eyes are drooping and I feel drained

questions.text: If someone asked you a difficult question right now, you would:

options.text: Think clearly and respond without stress
Feel prepared — I'd handle it confidently
Smile and take my time, no rush
Feel anxious and worry about giving the wrong answer
Struggle to focus — my mind feels foggy

questions.text: What best describes your breathing right now?

options.text: Slow and natural — I'm at peace
Normal and steady — I'm in control
Deep and easy — I feel comfortable
Shallow or fast — I feel a bit on edge
Slow but heavy — like sighing a lot

questions.text: How would you describe your thoughts right now?

options.text: Quiet and settled — my mind is clear
Organized and focused — I know what I'm doing
Wandering pleasantly — no pressure to think
Racing or worried — I can't stop overthinking
Slow and scattered — hard to concentrate

questions.text: If the session started right now with something challenging, you'd feel:

options.text: Ready — I'm in a good headspace
Confident — bring it on, I'm prepared
Easygoing — I'll go with the flow
Nervous — I hope I don't mess up
Unmotivated — I just want to rest

questions.text: How did you sleep last night?

options.text: Peacefully — I woke up feeling good
Well enough — I feel sharp and alert
Great — I feel refreshed and easy
Poorly — I was anxious or had bad dreams
Not enough — I still feel exhausted

questions.text: What's your energy level right now (1 being lowest)?

options.text: 7/10 — Steady and balanced
8/10 — High and focused
6/10 — Comfortable, not too high not too low
5/10 — Nervous energy, not the good kind
2-3/10 — Running on empty

questions.text: If you had to describe your current mood in one word:

options.text: Peaceful
Focused
Chill
Anxious
Exhausted

questions.text: How do you feel about being here today?

options.text: Content — I'm happy to be here
Motivated — I came here to learn
Laid back — open to whatever happens
Worried — I hope I can keep up
Low energy — I wish I could be resting

questions.text: What would help you most right now?

options.text: Nothing — I'm in a good place already
A clear goal to work towards
Some music or a comfortable space
Reassurance that it's okay to make mistakes
A short break or something energizing

Calm.label: Calm & Centered
Calm.description: You are in a peaceful, balanced state. Your mind is clear and your body is relaxed. This is an excellent state for learning — you can absorb information well and think clearly.
Calm.forFacilitator: This student is ready to learn. They can handle complex tasks and deep thinking. Great time for challenging content.

Composed.label: Composed & Focused
Composed.description: You are alert, organized, and ready to take on challenges. Your mind is sharp and you feel in control. This is a peak learning state — you're prepared to tackle anything.
Composed.forFacilitator: This student is highly engaged and ready for active learning. Give them leadership roles, challenges, or problem-solving tasks.

Relaxed.label: Relaxed & Easy-going
Relaxed.description: You feel comfortable and at ease. There's no pressure or tension. You're open to learning but in a laid-back way. Good for absorbing information, though high-pressure tasks might feel unwelcome.
Relaxed.forFacilitator: This student is comfortable but may need gentle engagement. Use interactive activities to raise energy slightly without adding pressure.

Frightened.label: Anxious & On Edge
Frightened.description: You're feeling some nervousness or worry right now. Your body might be tense and your thoughts may be racing. It's harder to learn in this state because your brain is in 'alert mode' rather than 'learning mode'.
Frightened.forFacilitator: This student needs safety and reassurance. Start with easy wins, create a no-judgment environment, use ice-breakers, and explicitly say it's okay to make mistakes.

Tired.label: Tired & Low Energy
Tired.description: Your energy is low and your mind feels foggy. You might be physically or mentally exhausted. Learning is difficult when you're running on empty — your brain needs energy to process new information.
Tired.forFacilitator: This student needs energizers. Start with a short physical activity, provide a break, use highly interactive/visual content, and avoid long lectures. Consider shorter learning bursts.
